subject: Faulkner Health - SLA credit structure & migration maintenance carveout
messages:
From: Ava Lin <ava.lin@faulknerhealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@faulknerhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: SLA questions for migration window / credit structure

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we prepare for our platform migration (planned Q1), our security and procurement teams have a couple of asks around the SLA that are blockers for the contract:

- We understand Redwood's baseline uptime is listed in the template, but we need clarity on how monthly credits are calculated for partial-month outages during the migration window.
- We also need an explicit carveout for scheduled migration maintenance: our migrations will require longer planned windows (up to 8 hours in a single weekend) for DNS and DB cutover. Can Redwood provide an exception path and an agreed temporary uptime floor for that 90-day migration period?
- Latency SLOs: our front-end requires 99th percentile p95+p99 latency targets for generation calls; what are the measurable latency bands you will commit to, and are those tied to credits?

I can share a redline from procurement if that helps. Attached is our internal requirements doc for the migration.

Looking for a short call to align — are you available next Tuesday 11/16?

Thanks,
Ava Lin
Director of Platform
Faulkner Health

Attachment: Faulkner_migration_requirements.pdf (reference only)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Ava Lin <ava.lin@faulknerhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@faulknerhealth.com, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA questions for migration window / credit structure

Ava — thanks for the clear summary. We can definitely accommodate a migration carveout; wanted to outline an operationally-safe approach so we don't create open-ended availability risk for other customers. Proposed items below:

1) Temporary availability floor: For the 90-day migration window, Redwood can set an agreed availability floor of 99.85% (versus our standard hosted SLA of 99.95%). This would be a temporary amendment that automatically reverts after the migration period unless extended by mutual written agreement.

2) Scheduled maintenance carveout: Planned maintenance windows for the migration (up to 8 hours in a single weekend) will be pre-scheduled and excluded from uptime calculations provided Faulkner gives >= 7 days notice and coordinates a single maintenance window per migration weekend. Any additional unannounced downtime during that period remains subject to standard credits.

3) Credit calculation: We propose a tiered monthly credit schedule tied to monthly availability bands (see attached monthly-credit-table.xlsx):
   - 99.95%+ : no credits
   - 99.50% - 99.95% : credit = 10% of monthly bill (pro-rated to affected service hours)
   - 99.00% - 99.50% : credit = 25% of monthly bill
   - <99.00% : credit = 50% of monthly bill
   Cap: credits capped at 75% of the monthly invoice.

4) Latency: We treat latency separately from availability. For generation endpoints, we can commit to a 99th percentile latency target of 350ms for standard models and 700ms for larger-context models, measured at the edge. Latency misses will not generate monetary credits in this proposal but will trigger operational remediation (priority SLT paging) and a 1:1 credit discussion if regressions persist across two consecutive months.

I'll attach a written amendment and the credit table for review — looping in Laura (legal) to confirm contract language. If this framing looks acceptable, we can prepare a short amendment and schedule the migration carveout in the contract.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Faulkner_SLA_Redwood_Proposal_v1.pdf, monthly-credit-table.xlsx

From: Ava Lin <ava.lin@faulknerhealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@faulknerhealth.com, Mike Gorsky <mg@faulknerhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T11:22:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA questions for migration window / credit structure

Rafael — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from procurement/security:

- The temporary floor of 99.85% is acceptable in principle, but procurement wants the credit calculus to be more granular during the migration (i.e., prorated to the exact affected service hours during the maintenance window rather than full-month pro-ration).
- The cap at 75% is ok, but we need an explicit carveout for multi-hour single-event outages during migration: if a single migration activity causes >4 hours of cumulative unplanned downtime in that weekend (outside the scheduled window), Faulkner wants a bump in credits to 90% of the prorated monthly charge for that service.
- Latency: we understand your remediation-first stance. However, our platform requires a firm p99 target for user-facing token completions. Can Redwood commit to operational credits (non-monetary) such as service credits + prioritized engineering support if latency regressions exceed the p99 target for >72 continuous hours?

Would you and legal consider the following edits: prorated credits by the hour for migration-related events, a single-event breach uplift clause (bump to 90%), and a defined escalation path (SLT contact + 4-hour response SLA) for latency incidents?

If we can get agreement on those three, procurement can move to signature next week.

Regards,
Ava

Attachment: Faulkner_procurement_redline_20261118.pdf (will follow if needed)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T08:03:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Faulkner - migration carveout asks (procurement redline)

Laura / Ben — forwarding Faulkner's asks. High level: they want hourly prorating for migration-related credits, a one-off single-event uplift to 90% for >4h unplanned outage during migration weekend, and operational credits + guaranteed SLT escalation for latency regressions >72h.

My read: hourly prorating and a one-time uplift are workable but increase financial exposure; we should limit the uplift to the migration period and require (a) detailed post-mortem, (b) that the outage is confirmed to be Redwood service-related (not DNS/CDN/partner), and (c) a mutual cap across the migration period (suggest cap = 90% of prorated monthly bill but limited to one event).

For latency escalation: I can agree to the SLT page + prioritized engineering support. I recommend we avoid automatic monetary credits for latency unless the defect persists across two months (consistent with how we treat performance regressions today). Instead offer a credit-for-remediation clause: if remediation does not meet agreed timelines, then a discretionary credit up to 25% of the impacted service bill for that month.

As next steps: Laura, can you draft a short amendment with: temporary floor 99.85% for 90 days; hourly prorated methodology for migration-related downtime; single-event uplift to 90% with the forensic/one-event cap language; and the latency escalation + remediation-credit trigger? Ben — would you run a quick exposure calc if we accepted the uplift (one-time cap at 90% prorated) and the 75% overall cap?

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Ava Lin <ava.lin@faulknerhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@faulknerhealth.com, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T16:42:00Z
Subject: Final: migration carveout amendment & credit schedule (redlined)

Ava — thanks for the patience while we ran this internally. Attached is a short amendment (PDF) and an updated monthly-credit-table.xlsx that incorporates the points we discussed. Summary of changes from our side:

- Temporary availability floor of 99.85% for a defined 90-day migration period (dates to be populated in the amendment). This reverts automatically unless both parties sign an extension.
- Hourly prorating for migration-related scheduled windows and for accidental migration-related downtime. Credits will be calculated against the exact number of affected service hours during the billing period.
- Single-event uplift: If a single unplanned outage during the migration weekend exceeds 4 cumulative hours and is attributable to Redwood, the customer will receive a one-time credit equal to 90% of the prorated monthly charge for the impacted service, subject to a post-incident forensic review and confirmation. This uplift is limited to one event during the migration period.
- Monthly credit bands remain tiered with a hard cap at 75% of the monthly invoice for routine outages; the uplift is a carveout limited as stated above.
- Latency: We will provide SLT escalation + prioritized engineering support for p99 latency regressions exceeding 72 continuous hours. If remediation timelines in the amendment are not met, Faulkner will be eligible to request a remediation credit (up to 25% of the impacted service bill for that month) subject to review.

If this matches what procurement needs, please confirm and we will send the formal amendment for signature and update the contract. If you want any language tweaks, Laura is on the thread and can incorporate them into the PDF.

Warmly,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Faulkner_SLA_Redwood_Proposal_v1.pdf, monthly-credit-table.xlsx
